thesis: The episode introduces Bill Spitz, a seasoned allocator who managed Vanderbilt University's endowment starting in 1985, a time when most portfolios were relatively conservative and simple despite Vanderbilt being an early player in alternatives. Spitz explains that he transitioned from Wall Street to the endowment world because he realized he was not a skilled stock or bond picker but rather possessed a passion for broad macro themes and the skills of a manager of managers.
